title: Chanel No. 5
blurb: Launched in 1921, the aldehyde-laden floral that became the most famous perfume in the world.

title: Shalimar
blurb: Guerlain's 1925 vanilla-and-bergamot oriental, named after the gardens of a Mughal emperor.

title: Old Spice
blurb: The nautical-themed aftershave in the ivory bottle that generations of grandfathers smelled of.

title: Opium
blurb: Yves Saint Laurent's heady 1977 spice-and-amber scent, as controversial as it was successful.

title: CK One
blurb: The clean citrus fragrance of 1994, sold in a plain flask and worn by everyone regardless of gender.

title: Attar
blurb: A concentrated perfume oil distilled from flowers, herbs or woods into sandalwood, with no alcohol at all.

title: Pomander
blurb: A ball of perfumes, or an orange studded with cloves, once carried to ward off bad air.

title: Ambergris
blurb: A waxy substance from sperm whales that washes ashore and was long prized for fixing perfume.

title: D.S. & Durga
blurb: Founded by an architect and a musician, D.S. & Durga started from scratch in Brooklyn and, in its own words, makes everything it loves into fragrance.

title: Juniper Ridge
about: Wild fragrances distilled in Oakland, California
blurb: Juniper Ridge crafts natural fragrances and essential oils from scratch by steam distillation in its Oakland, California workshop.

title: Régime des Fleurs
about: Perfumes inspired by nature, history and art
blurb: A New York perfume house making scents inspired by nature, history and art.

title: Gulabsingh Johrimal
blurb: A traditional perfumery founded in 1816 in the lanes of Old Delhi by Lala Gulab Singh and his son Johrimal, still making attars and incense.

title: Phool
blurb: Phool makes charcoal-free incense sticks and cones from flowers offered at temples, which would otherwise go to waste.
